item.text:
Continuation completed for selected Chapter 1B without scoring.

New defensible source-claim units:

- `WEB-1B-016` — BAPETEN conducted IAEA safeguards inspections on 12–16 June 2023 under Indonesia’s NPT Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement. Supports `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`; target-period, administration-level attribution. [BAPETEN safeguards report](https://bapeten.go.id/berita/inspeksi-safeguards-iaea-tahun-2023-130559)

- `WEB-1B-017` — Indonesia participated in the 2023 Convention on Nuclear Safety review meeting and presented its national safety report. Supports `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`; target-period institutional evidence. [BAPETEN CNS review report](https://bapeten.go.id/berita/bapeten-pimpin-delegasi--indonesia-dalam-review-meeting-of-the-convention-on-nuclear-safety-2023-124033)

- `WEB-1B-018` — Indonesia’s 2023 national safety report states that it had three operating research reactors but no nuclear power plant, with BAPETEN conducting regulatory review, inspection, emergency exercises, and incident reporting. Supports `1B.3`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`; target-period technical evidence. [IAEA-hosted Indonesian national report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/24/01/9th_rm_national_report_cns_indonesia.pdf), pp. 5, 42–48, 61–63.

- `WEB-1B-019` — BAPETEN and IAEA conducted a May 2023 expert mission reviewing Indonesia’s nuclear-security detection architecture, including radiation portal monitors at Semarang, Bitung, and Makassar. Supports `1B.3`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`; target-period implementation evidence. [BAPETEN expert-mission report](https://www.bapeten.go.id/berita/opening-meeting-expert-mission-to-review-detection-measures-and-sustainability-of-nuclear-security-detection-architecture-203518?lang=en)

- `WEB-1B-020` — BAPETEN and IAEA held a December 2023 regional training course and practical exercise on nuclear-security detection and alarm assessment in Yogyakarta. Supports `1B.6`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`; target-period preparedness evidence. [BAPETEN–IAEA detection exercise](https://www.bapeten.go.id/berita/pentingnya-deteksi-keamanan-nuklir-bapeten-gandeng-iaea-gelar-regional-training-course-144527)

Contrary and limitation findings:

- The 2023 record documents civilian safeguards, safety regulation, detection architecture, and emergency preparedness; it does not establish covert nuclear capability, military command-and-control, or a nuclear crisis.
- The IAEA/BAPETEN material is strongest for declared civilian activities and institutional controls. It cannot independently exclude undisclosed capability.
- The national safety report records that responders’ coordination and capability still required improvement, so preparedness should not be treated as complete.
- No defensible evidence was found for `1B.5` beyond the continuing absence of a documented Indonesian nuclear-weapons posture; that absence remains non-evidentiary context.
